explainer.identity_text:
• Real Type (Magic Bytes): Reveals the true file format even if an attacker modified the extension (e.g. an .exe disguised as .pdf).
• Hashes (SHA-256, MD5, SHA-1): Unique and tamper-proof digital fingerprints. If a single byte changes, the entire hash changes. This allows verifying file integrity against known malware or legitimate software databases.
• Imphash: Import table fingerprint, used to link this file to other variants from the same malware family.
explainer.pe_title: What is the PE (Portable Executable) Structure?
explainer.pe_text:
• PE Format: Standard format for all Windows executables (.exe) and dynamic libraries (.dll).
• Sections: Program memory compartments (.text for code, .data for variables, .rsrc for resources). A section marked both Writable and Executable (W+X) is a critical anomaly often used for runtime code injection.
• Authenticode Signature: Indicates whether the binary was cryptographically signed by a verified publisher. The absence of a signature is very common in malicious software.
• MITRE ATT&CK APIs: System functions called by the program that expose its capabilities (process injection, autostart persistence, network telemetry).
explainer.entropy_text:
• Shannon Entropy: Measures the randomness of data on a scale from 0.000 to 8.000.
• Standard Code (4.0 to 6.5): Plain text, standard compiled instructions.
• Very High Entropy (> 7.200): Encrypted, compressed, or packed data. Malware authors use packers (UPX, VMProtect, custom stubs) to hide malicious code from static scanners.
• Block Entropy: Slices the file into 16 KB chunks to visually pinpoint hidden encrypted payloads.
explainer.strings_title: What are IOCs and String Extraction?
explainer.strings_text:
• Strings: Plaintext sequences embedded in the binary (URLs, commands, paths, messages).
• IOC (Indicator of Compromise): Concrete forensic evidence of malicious activity: C2 server IP addresses, malicious download URLs, autostart registry keys, or stealthy PowerShell commands.
• Purpose: Immediately reveals who the program tries to contact or what system commands it attempts to run.
explainer.yara_text:
• YARA: The global industry standard used by SOC analysts and threat researchers to detect and classify malware.
• Mechanism: Each rule describes binary or textual patterns unique to a known threat family (WannaCry, RedLine Stealer, Mimikatz, etc.).
• Alert: When a rule triggers, the file contains the exact technical DNA of a known malware or offensive tool.
